name: PA-13
label: Safe R

key_factors: R+23 partisan lean of the district
Joyce's large financial advantage ($3.8M cash vs $16K)
Incumbent running with no expert raters flagging the race
model.rationale: The district's R+23 lean, Joyce's incumbency, and his overwhelming fundraising edge leave Farnham with no visible path; prediction markets agree at roughly 3% for Democrats. No polls or expert ratings suggest any reason to move off the fundamentals.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending against Joyce or a major scandal would be the only realistic route to narrowing this race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Pennsylvania's 13th District is deeply Republican territory, and incumbent John Joyce is seeking another term with every structural advantage. The seat's partisan lean sits around R+23, and Joyce has built a war chest of roughly $3.8 million, dwarfing Democrat Beth Farnham's $16,000 on hand. No outside groups have invested in the race on either side, and no expert rating organizations list it as competitive.

Prediction markets give Democrats only about a 3% chance, consistent with the district's fundamentals. Farnham's minimal fundraising means she will struggle to communicate with voters at all, let alone overcome a two-decade-scale partisan gap. The race is expected to remain firmly in Republican hands with little genuine contestation.
